record.file_problem: none; the full post and comments are present.
record.tranche_reason: The post makes a specific conceptual case that representational convergence is contingent on shared pressures and environments, and can be fragile under architectural or optimization changes. It does not run an empirical test; its illustrative vision result is attributed to another paper.
record.gate_note: The post discusses and interprets findings attributed to Fort et al. (arXiv:2408.05446), including adversarial divergence and improved human alignment with multi-resolution training. Those are cited results, not results produced by this post, so they are not rows. Other examples and predictions are conceptual rather than measured outcomes.
record.test_reason: A conceptual post with no experiments of its own. It makes a specific argument against V7's 'common model of reality' reading: convergence comes from shared learning pressures and environments, is partial, and is contingent on architecture. Its only empirical illustration, multi-resolution training in vision, is cited from Fort et al. (arXiv:2408.05446), so it is not a row. The argument bears mainly on V7, and on how V1 is interpreted rather than whether it holds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. Add two points. First, the author holds that most evidence for natural abstractions or the Platonic representation hypothesis is equally explained by convergence under shared pressures, which is the weaker claim. Second, human-AI abstraction alignment may be extensive yet partial and fragile under strong optimization.
